# Accuracy: np, lite build

Measured on `np-places-lite.tgd` (np 2026.11.0) against the labelled sample of [`tests/golden/np-places.csv`](../../../tests/golden/np-places.csv): 299 places drawn by class and terrain, 222 marked with a settlement, 77 marked as showing none.

## How the truth was made

The labels were made **by AI agents, not by people with local knowledge** ([accuracy labels](../../../docs/02-research/notes/accuracy-labels.md), D-209). Each agent saw a Copernicus Sentinel-2 image (10 m pixels) of the place's surroundings with the points of open building-footprint datasets on top, and a hint of the place's kilometre cell, and marked the centre of the built-up area carrying the name. Nothing from the forge's own output was shown. There are no names on the images, so where two clusters are alike the label is a judgement; the agreement of a second, blind pass below is the measure of that noise. A people-made set replaces this one when it exists.

## Vertical

The pack's elevation of each place against the terrain height the same pack gives at the label, metres: the part of the vertical error that comes from the point's position, since both are read from one DEM. The DEM's own error against ICESat-2 is measured separately ([S6](../../../docs/02-research/benches/s6-elevation.md)). Target (D-062): P90 ≤ 50 m for the two together.

| Stratum | Places | P50 | P90 | Within 50 m |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| hamlet, hill | 44 | 14 | 137 | 66% |
| hamlet, lowland | 56 | 1 | 6 | 100% |
| town, hill | 23 | 12 | 79 | 83% |
| town, lowland | 4 | 4 | 10 | 100% |
| village, hill | 36 | 45 | 226 | 56% |
| village, lowland | 59 | 2 | 10 | 100% |
| **all** | 222 | 3 | 98 | 84% |

## Agreement of two blind passes

60 places were labelled twice, the second time by another agent on mirrored chips with a moved centre. Both marked a settlement for 41 (68%), both marked none for 8, and they disagreed on whether there is one for 11 (18%).

| Both marked | n | P50 (m) | P90 (m) | Within 150 m | Within 500 m |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| distance between the two marks | 41 | 63 | 385 | 63% | 90% |

## Reading these numbers

- A label is itself uncertain by about the agreement distances above, so a P90 below them cannot be shown with this set; the hill target of 150 m is finer than the labels.
- The same noise enters the vertical table: on a hillside a label a few hundred metres off reads a terrain height tens of metres off, so the hill rows are an upper bound on the error from position.
- Places marked as showing no settlement (scattered houses, no buildings in the footprint data) are not scored: the sample says nothing about where those names belong.
- The sample is small per stratum; a stratum of under 10 places is a hint, not a measurement.
